literal: " When the imperial carriage campaigned south, he was made Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Qing Province.
idiomatic: " On the southern campaign he was made Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Qing Province.

literal: The edict to Yu said: "The charge of the coastal regions—therefore only a worthy of the clan.
idiomatic: The edict to Yu said, "The coastal charge belongs only to a worthy of the clan.

literal: Only wine, only fields—can you not be warned!
idiomatic: Only wine, only fields—will you not take warning!"

literal: When Xuanwu took the throne, Yu was transferred to Governor of Sizhou.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne Yu was transferred to Governor of Sizhou.

literal: When the emperor took charge of government he was brought inside and personally invested as Minister of Education.
idiomatic: When the emperor took charge of government Yu was brought inside and personally invested as Minister of Education.

literal: He asked to be Minister of Works and it was granted.
idiomatic: He asked to be Minister of Works and it was granted.

literal: Earlier Yu had debauched the wife of the Extraordinary Attendant Feng Junxing and went out at night in secret.
idiomatic: Earlier Yu had debauched the wife of Extraordinary Attendant Feng Junxing and went out at night in secret.

literal: Junxing struck him; for many days he kept it secret, and he died in his residence.
idiomatic: Junxing struck him; for many days he kept it hidden, and he died in his residence.

literal: Xuanwu personally came to mourn; he was posthumously made Minister of Education with posthumous title Hui.
idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu came in person to mourn; he was posthumously made Minister of Education with the posthumous title Hui.

literal: His son Gong inherited—this was Emperor Jiemin.
idiomatic: His son Gong inherited—this was Emperor Jiemin.

literal: Gong's elder brother Xin, styled Qingle, was coarse by nature and fond of hawks and dogs.
idiomatic: Gong's elder brother Xin, styled Qingle, was coarse by nature and fond of hawks and dogs.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang he was enfeoffed Prince of Pei commandery, later Prince of Huaiyang.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was enfeoffed Prince of Pei commandery, later Prince of Huaiyang.

literal: Under Xiaowu he was made Grand Preceptor and Commander-in-Chief, again enfeoffed Prince of Guangling, Grand Tutor, and Governor of Sizhou, then soon removed as Grand Marshal.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu he was made Grand Preceptor and Commander-in-Chief, again enfeoffed Prince of Guangling, Grand Tutor, and Governor of Sizhou, then soon made Grand Marshal.

literal: When Xiaowu entered Guanzhong, Xin entrusted an envoy to reach Chang'an and was made Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guanzhong Xin sent an envoy to reach Chang'an and was made Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Among the imperial kin of the Zhongxing era Xin received the most honored treatment; from Prince of Guangping and the other princes, all were below him.
idiomatic: Among the imperial kin of the Zhongxing restoration Xin received the highest honors; from Prince of Guangping downward all ranked below him.

literal: He was again made Grand Clan Master, promoted to Grand Steward of the Tomb, and Commander-in-Chief of the Central Army.
idiomatic: He was again made Grand Clan Master, promoted Grand Steward of the Tomb, and Commander-in-Chief of the Central Army.

literal: In the Datong era he was Pillar of State, Grand General, and Grand Tutor.
idiomatic: In the Datong era he was Pillar of State, Grand General, and Grand Tutor.

literal: Emperor Wen said to Xin: "You have thrice been Grand Tutor and twice Grand Preceptor—from antiquity among subjects, I have never heard this example."
idiomatic: Emperor Wen said to Xin, "You have thrice been Grand Tutor and twice Grand Preceptor—from antiquity among subjects I have never heard such an example."

literal: Xin declined with apologies only.
idiomatic: Xin declined with apologies only.

literal: Later he was made Minister of Education.
idiomatic: He was later made Minister of Education.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gongdi's reign he was transferred to Grand Chancellor.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Gongdi's reign he was transferred to Grand Chancellor.

literal: He died; posthumous title Rong.
idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Rong.

literal: Xin loved to build estates and planted much; the capital's famous fruits all came from his gardens.
idiomatic: Xin loved to build estates and planted widely; the capital's famous fruits all came from his gardens.

literal: Those he brought in and his staff were none of them men of stature; the age despised him.
idiomatic: Those he brought in and his staff were none of them men of stature, and the age despised him.

literal: Prince of Gaoyang Yong, styled Simu, in youth was unconventional and unsteady.
idiomatic: Prince of Gaoyang Yong, styled Simu, in youth was unconventional and unsteady.

literal: Xiaowen said: 'I also cannot measure this boy's depth; yet seeing him sincere and plain by nature, perhaps in years and capacity he will mature late.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said, "I too cannot measure this boy's depth; yet seeing him sincere and plain by nature, perhaps in years and capacity he will mature late.

literal: " In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed Prince of Yingchuan.
idiomatic: " In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed Prince of Yingchuan.

literal: Some said Yong treated scholars to build reputation; Yong said: "I am the Son of Heaven's son, rank among princes—what use is reputation?
idiomatic: Some said Yong cultivated scholars to build reputation; Yong said, "I am the Son of Heaven's son and rank among princes—what use is reputation?

literal: " He was changed to Prince of Gaoyang.
idiomatic: " He was changed to Prince of Gaoyang.

literal: Later he was made Governor of Xiang Province.
idiomatic: He was later made Governor of Xiang Province.

literal: The emperor admonished him: "The way of governing is both easy and hard.
idiomatic: The emperor admonished him, "Governing is both easy and hard.

literal: If the person is upright, without giving orders things are done—therefore it is easy;
idiomatic: If the person is upright, without giving orders things are done—therefore it is easy;

literal: if the person is not upright, though orders are given they are not followed—therefore it is said to be hard."
idiomatic: if the person is not upright, though orders are given they are not followed—therefore it is hard."

literal: At the beginning of Xuanwu he was transferred to Governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was transferred to Governor of Ji Province.

literal: In the two provinces Yong had slight reputation; he entered court as Governor of Sizhou.
idiomatic: In the two provinces Yong had some reputation; he entered court as Governor of Sizhou.

literal: When the emperor visited Yong's residence, all used family ritual.
idiomatic: When the emperor visited Yong's residence they used full family ritual.

literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works, then Grand Commandant, and made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Works, then Grand Commandant, and made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

literal: Soon he was made Grand Guardian, retaining Grand Commandant and Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
idiomatic: Soon he was made Grand Guardian, retaining Grand Commandant and Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign an edict ordered Yong to dwell in the Western Cypress Hall of Taiji, consult on great affairs, and gave him twenty trusted men.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign an edict ordered Yong to dwell in the Western Cypress Hall of Taiji, consult on great affairs, and gave him twenty trusted men.

literal: Another edict made Yong Grand Clan Master, promoted to Grand Tutor and Attendant-in-Ordinary, retaining Grand Commandant; a separate edict had the Directorate of Works build the National University temple for Yong to dwell in.
idiomatic: Another edict made Yong Grand Clan Master and promoted him to Grand Tutor and Attendant-in-Ordinary while retaining Grand Commandant; a separate edict had the Directorate of Works build the National University temple for his residence.

literal: Commander of the Palace Guards Yu Zhong seized power and acted as he pleased; Vice Director Guo Zuo urged Yong to remove him; Zhong forged an edict and killed Zuo and Director of the Masters of Writing Pei Zhi, deposed Yong and sent him home as a prince.
idiomatic: Commander of the Palace Guards Yu Zhong seized power and acted as he pleased; Vice Director Guo Zuo urged Yong to remove him; Zhong forged an edict and killed Zuo and Director Pei Zhi, deposed Yong, and sent him home as a prince.

literal: When the court had great affairs they sent the Yellow Gate to consult him.
idiomatic: When the court had great affairs they sent the Yellow Gate to consult him.

literal: Zhong soon again forged an edict intending to kill Yong; he asked Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang, who refused—and he stopped.
idiomatic: Zhong soon forged another edict intending to kill Yong; he asked Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang, who refused, and he stopped.

literal: Before long Empress Dowager Ling held court and sent Zhong out as Governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: Before long Empress Dowager Ling held court and sent Zhong out as Governor of Ji Province.

literal: Yong memorialized exposing Zhong's crimes and stating that he himself could not correct them, asking to return to private life.
idiomatic: Yong memorialized exposing Zhong's crimes, confessing that he could not correct them, and asking to return to private life.

literal: Empress Dowager Ling was moved by Zhong's merit in protecting her and did not inquire into his crimes.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling was moved by Zhong's merit in protecting her and did not inquire into his crimes.

literal: Yong was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Preceptor and took charge of Sizhou.
idiomatic: Yong was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Preceptor and took charge of Sizhou.

literal: Yong memorialized asking that from princes and dukes downward concubines of low rank all be forbidden woven brocade, gold, jade, and pearls—violators to be judged by violating the edict;
idiomatic: Yong memorialized that from princes and dukes downward all low-rank concubines be forbidden woven brocade, gold, jade, and pearls—violators judged by violating the edict;

literal: slave girls must not wear damask or brocade patterns, only plain silk;
idiomatic: slave girls must not wear patterned damask or brocade, only plain silk;

literal: male slaves only cloth garments, and none may use gold or silver for hairpins and belts—violators receive a hundred strokes.
idiomatic: male slaves only cloth garments, and none may use gold or silver for hairpins and belts—violators receive a hundred strokes.

literal: The empress dowager followed it, but could not keep it long.
idiomatic: The empress dowager agreed, but could not keep it long.

literal: An edict allowed Yong to ride a drawn carriage in and out of the side gates, and with his original office to record the Masters of Writing; morning and evening he attended lectures.
idiomatic: An edict allowed Yong to ride a drawn carriage through the side gates and, with his original office, to record the Masters of Writing; morning and evening he attended lectures.

literal: When Emperor Ming took charge of government an edict allowed Yong to ride in and out of the Grand Marshal Gate and promoted him to Chancellor.
idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took charge of government an edict allowed Yong to ride through the Grand Marshal Gate and promoted him to Chancellor.

literal: Another edict followed the Taihe precedent of Prince Jian of Qi commandery Shun: after court, he was invited to sit and received special bowing and prostration.
idiomatic: Another edict followed the Taihe precedent of Prince Jian of Qi commandery Shun: after court he was invited to sit and received special bowing and prostration.

literal: He oversaw internal and external affairs and with Yuan Cha jointly decided ordinary government.
idiomatic: He oversaw internal and external affairs and with Yuan Cha jointly decided ordinary government.

literal: Annual salary grain reached forty thousand piculs; performing girls filled the rooms; splendor and honor such that his brothers could not match.
idiomatic: Annual salary grain reached forty thousand piculs; performing girls filled his rooms; splendor and honor his brothers could not match.

literal: After his primary consort the Lu clan died, he took as consort the younger sister of Boling Cui Xian and wished to make her consort.
idiomatic: After his primary consort Lady Lu died he took as consort the younger sister of Boling Cui Xian and wished to make her his princess consort.

literal: At the beginning of Xuanwu, because Cui Xian's house was called Eastern Cui in the age, of low land and weak standing, it was difficult; only after long delay was permission granted.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign, because Cui Xian's house was called Eastern Cui in the age and was of low land and weak standing, the match was resisted; only after long delay was permission granted.

literal: After Yan-chang he neglected the Cui clan, kept her in a separate chamber under close guard, giving only food and clothing.
idiomatic: After Yan-chang he neglected the Cui clan, kept her in a separate chamber under close guard, giving only food and clothing.

literal: Before long Lady Cui died violently; many said Yong beat her to death.
idiomatic: Before long Lady Cui died violently; many said Yong beat her to death.

literal: Empress Dowager Ling had granted him her female performers but had not yet sent them.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling had granted him her female performers but had not yet sent them.

literal: Yong sent his eunuch Ding E in person to the inner palace, selected four on his own authority, and took them back to his residence.
idiomatic: Yong sent his eunuch Ding E in person to the inner palace, selected four on his own authority, and took them back to his residence.

literal: The empress dowager reproached his usurpation and halted it.
idiomatic: The empress dowager reproached his usurpation and halted it.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang he was killed at Heyin.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.

literal: Posthumously given the Acting Yellow Battle-axe and Chancellor; posthumous title Wenmu.
idiomatic: He was posthumously given the Acting Yellow Battle-axe and Chancellor with the posthumous title Wenmu.

literal: Yong's insight was shallow and he had no learning; though he stood at the head of court, he was not pushed by the mood of the time.
idiomatic: Yong's insight was shallow and he had no learning; though he stood at the head of court, the mood of the time did not favor him.

literal: From Xiping onward court government fell into disorder.
idiomatic: From the Xiping era onward court government fell into disorder.

literal: When Prince of Qinghe Yi died, Yuan Cha monopolized government; the realm's great blame fell on him.
idiomatic: When Prince of Qinghe Yi died, Yuan Cha monopolized government and the realm's great blame fell on Yong.

literal: His eldest son Tai, styled Chang, had some reputation in the time and held the office of Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he was killed with Yong at the same time.
idiomatic: His eldest son Tai, styled Chang, had some reputation in the time and served as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he was killed with Yong at the same time.

literal: Posthumously made Grand Commandant and Prince of Gaoyang; posthumous title Wen.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant and Prince of Gaoyang with the posthumous title Wen.

literal: His son Bin inherited.
idiomatic: His son Bin inherited.

literal: Bin, styled Shanji, held in succession Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Bin, styled Shanji, served in turn as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Bin had handsome bearing and a mild nature; in office he was very cautious and was quite favored by Qi Emperor Wenxiang.
idiomatic: Bin was handsome and mild; in office he was very cautious and was quite favored by Qi Emperor Wenxiang.

literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao, by precedent his rank was reduced to Duke of Gaoyang county and he was made Grand Master for the Palace with Glory Equal to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao, by precedent his rank was reduced to Duke of Gaoyang county and he was made Grand Master for the Palace with Glory Equal to the Three Excellencies.

literal: In the second year, returning from campaigning against the Khitan with Wenxuan, at the White Wolf River he was sentenced to death for a crime.
idiomatic: In the second year, returning from campaigning against the Khitan with Emperor Wenxuan, at the White Wolf River he was sentenced to death for a crime.

literal: Prince of Pengcheng Xie, styled Yanhe, from youth was precocious; in disposition he was unlike others.
idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Xie, styled Yanhe, was precocious from youth and unlike others in disposition.

literal: In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed Prince of Shiping and made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed Prince of Shiping and made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

literal: Xie was born and his mother Lady Pan died; that year Xianwen died.
idiomatic: Xie was born and his mother Lady Pan died; that year Emperor Xianwen died.

literal: When he came to understanding he petitioned to observe mourning; Empress Dowager Wenming did not permit it.
idiomatic: When he came to understanding he petitioned to observe mourning for her; Empress Dowager Wenming did not permit it.

literal: He therefore ruined his appearance in grief, observed heart-mourning three years, and did not take part in auspicious celebrations.
idiomatic: He therefore wasted his appearance in grief, observed heart-mourning for three years, and took no part in auspicious celebrations.

literal: Xiaowen marveled greatly.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen marveled greatly.

literal: Quick and devoted to learning, he elegantly loved composing literature.
idiomatic: Quick and devoted to learning, he elegantly loved composing literature.

literal: On long duty inside the forbidden quarters he took part in deciding great military and civil affairs; of the myriad tasks none did not involve him.
idiomatic: On long duty inside the forbidden quarters he took part in deciding great military and civil affairs; none of the myriad tasks passed without him.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south he took charge of the imperial clan army and guarded close at hand.
idiomatic: On the southern campaign he took charge of the imperial clan army and guarded close at hand.

literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before, and changed to Prince of Pengcheng.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before, and changed to Prince of Pengcheng.

literal: The emperor ascended the Jincheng ramparts, looked back and saw behind the hall paulownia and bamboo, and said: "The phoenix will not perch except on the paulownia, will not eat except bamboo fruit.
idiomatic: The emperor ascended the Jincheng ramparts, looked back, and saw paulownia and bamboo behind the hall. He said, "The phoenix will not perch except on paulownia and will not eat except bamboo fruit.

literal: Now paulownia and bamboo are both lush—can the phoenix descend?
idiomatic: Now paulownia and bamboo are both lush—can the phoenix descend?

literal: " Xie said: "The phoenix comes in response to virtue—how can paulownia and bamboo make it descend?
idiomatic: " Xie said, "The phoenix comes in response to virtue—how can paulownia and bamboo make it descend?

literal: " The emperor laughed and said: "I also did not expect it to descend."
idiomatic: " The emperor laughed and said, "I also did not expect it to descend."

literal: Later he feasted the attending ministers at the Clear Splendor Hall.
idiomatic: Later he feasted the attending ministers at the Clear Splendor Hall.

literal: The day grew late; they moved to beneath the fragrant trees at the Transforming Flow Pool.
idiomatic: The day grew late; they moved to beneath the fragrant trees at the Transforming Flow Pool.

literal: The emperor looked up at the paulownia leaves lush and said: "'Its paulownia, its chair-tree, its fruit hangs thick.
idiomatic: The emperor looked up at the lush paulownia leaves and said, "'Its paulownia, its chair-tree, its fruit hangs thick.

literal: The gracious gentleman—none is not admirable.'
idiomatic: The gracious gentleman—none is not admirable.'

literal: Now the worthies beneath the trees are enough to fill song and praise."
idiomatic: Now the worthies beneath the trees are enough to fill song and praise."

literal: He then ordered Secretariat Attendant Cui Guang to read the ministers' responsive poems for late spring.
idiomatic: He then ordered Secretariat Attendant Cui Guang to read the ministers' responsive poems for late spring.

literal: When they came to Xie's poem the emperor altered one character and said: "In the past Qi Xi recommended his son and the realm called it utmost fairness.
idiomatic: When they came to Xie's poem the emperor altered one character and said, "In the past Qi Xi recommended his son and the realm called it utmost fairness.

literal: Now seeing Xie's poem I know the Director's recommendation was not private."
idiomatic: Now seeing Xie's poem I know the director's recommendation was not private."

literal: Xie said: "Your servant shows this clumsy piece and thereby sees the holy court's favor; relying on the divine brush's correction I have worthy reputation."
idiomatic: Xie said, "Your servant shows this clumsy piece and thereby sees the holy court's favor; relying on the divine brush's correction I have worthy reputation."

literal: The emperor said: "Though one character is carved and polished, it is still the jade's original substance."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Though one character is carved and polished, it is still the jade's original substance."

literal: Xie said: 'The three hundred pieces of the Odes—a single phrase can cover them.
idiomatic: Xie said, "The three hundred pieces of the Odes—a single phrase can cover them.
